page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The statement
lines: The moment of inertia of a body about
any axis equals its moment of inertia
about a parallel axis through the
centre of mass, plus the product of the
mass and the square of the distance
steps.why: The statement-only form is how the new AP pattern asks theorems at 1-2 marks (Kepler’s law of areas was asked exactly this way in March 2026).
common_mistakes: Explaining the +Mr² by saying every particle moves farther from the new axis — false, some particles are closer to it. The theorem holds because the cross term Σm·(distance from the CM) sums to zero.

recall.must_convey: That I about any axis is I about the parallel axis through the CM plus mass times distance squared.
accept: parallel axis through the centre of mass

steps.label: The equation
steps.why: One line of symbols carries the whole theorem; the proof lives in the 4-mark form.
common_mistakes: Writing I = I₀ − Mr². The theorem always adds.

accept: I equals I naught plus M r squared
reject: I z equals I x plus I y
